Answer all questions. • For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet. • Write in soft pencil. • Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. • Do not use correction fluid. • Do not write on any bar codes. • You may use a calculator. INFORMATION • The total mark for this paper is 30. • Each correct answer will score one mark. • Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
A local council provides a tap for drinking water in a town. Would this make drinking water a free good?

options.A: No, because it is possible to exclude some people from using the tap.
options.B: No, because it requires the use of scarce resources.
options.C: Yes, because it is available to all passers-by.
options.D: Yes, because it is impossible to charge for it.

questions.questionText: Food prices in a country increased by 20% in three months due to an infectious virus. Which statement about the cause of this rise in food prices is normative?

options.A: Consumers were scared of running out of food.
options.B: Farm workers demanded higher wages to cover extra hours worked.
options.C: Supply of foreign food was reduced because of closed borders.
options.D: Transport costs increased by 10%.

questions.questionText: A doctor has very long working hours and a high level of stress. She can become a teacher instead of continuing as a doctor. What is the opportunity cost of choosing to continue as a doctor?

options.A: the risk of mistakes caused by tiredness
options.B: the possible costs of illness caused by high stress levels
options.C: the potential salary as a teacher
options.D: the retraining costs of becoming a teacher

questions.questionText: When will the demand curve for motorcycles shift to the left?

options.A: when the price of cars falls
options.B: when the price of motorcycles falls
options.C: when the tax on motorcycles rises
options.D: when the price of public transport rises

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand curve for housing. price D O quantity What is not assumed to remain constant when drawing this curve?

options.A: consumer incomes
options.B: expectations about future house prices
options.C: the price of houses
options.D: the rate of interest charged on loans for house purchase

questions.questionText: Which statement defines the price elasticity of supply?

options.A: It is a measure of how the price of a good responds to a change in the quantity supplied.
options.B: It is a measure of how the quantity supplied of a good responds to a change in its price.
options.C: It is a measure of how the supply of a good responds to a change in its cost of production.
options.D: It is a measure of how the supply of good X responds to a change in the price of good Y.

questions.questionText: Which products are likely to have a positive cross-elasticity of demand with tea?

options.A: biscuits and cakes
options.B: coffee and hot chocolate
options.C: cups and saucers
options.D: sugar and milk

questions.questionText: What does not cause a shift in the supply curve of cars?

options.A: a change in the car producers’ costs of production
options.B: a change in the price of fuel used by car owners
options.C: a change in the rate of sales tax on cars
options.D: a change in the wage rate of workers in the car industry

questions.questionText: When is the supply curve for a car manufacturing firm most likely to be price elastic?

options.A: when the firm finds it difficult to recruit new labour
options.B: when the firm has a large quantity of stock
options.C: when the firm is operating in the short run
options.D: when the firm is operating near to full capacity

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the market for electric steel-plated switches used in new houses. S price Y X D D O quantity What could not have caused the market equilibrium position to have changed from X to Y?

options.A: increasing the availability of loans for buying houses
options.B: granting a subsidy for producers of bricks
options.C: removing sales tax on electric switches
options.D: removing tariffs on imports of wood

questions.questionText: In mixed economies, what explains why the provision of certain goods and services will remain under government control?

options.A: The market system fails to provide public goods.
options.B: Management ideas are hampered by excessive bureaucracy.
options.C: Ownership of companies depends on the ease of buying shares.
options.D: The profit motive tends to improve efficiency in organisations.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the percentages of those on low pay and those on extremely low pay in a country from 1976 to 2012. A national minimum wage was introduced in 1999. % low paid introduction of minimum wage extremely low paid 1976 1980 1984 1988 1992 1996 2000 2004 2008 2012 year Which conclusion is consistent with the diagram?

options.A: The minimum wage helped the low paid more than the extremely low paid.
options.B: The minimum wage reduced the numbers of both low paid and extremely low paid.
options.C: The minimum wage reversed the trend in low pay of the previous 20 years.
options.D: The minimum wage was responsible for the largest reduction of low pay in the period.

questions.questionText: A concert arena has a fixed capacity that allows it to sell 10000 tickets for a concert. The current equilibrium price for a ticket is $10. The owners of the arena decide to set a minimum price for a ticket. Under which conditions will there be the most unsold tickets? minimum ticket price elasticity of price ($) demand for tickets

options.A: 11 inelastic
options.B: 11 elastic
options.C: 12 inelastic
options.D: 12 elastic

questions.questionText: A government announces its intention to reduce the level of transfer payments in the economy. Which statement made by the government is consistent with this intention?

options.A: There need to be more incentives for unemployed workers to seek jobs.
options.B: State pensions need to be increased.
options.C: The level of income tax needs to be raised.
options.D: The level of government expenditure needs to be increased.

questions.questionText: Assuming the demand for oil is price-inelastic, what will be the effect on demand-pull inflation and on cost-push inflation in an oil-importing country of an increase in the world price of oil? effect on demand-pull effect on cost-push inflation inflation

options.A: increase increase
options.B: increase reduce
options.C: reduce increase
options.D: reduce reduce

options.A: × 100 price index of imports price index of imports

options.C: × 100 total value of imports
options.D: total value of exports – total value of imports

questions.questionText: What is likely to cause an increase in the exchange rate of an economy?

options.A: an increase in demand-pull inflation
options.B: an increase in national income
options.C: a decision of the central bank to raise money supply
options.D: a discovery of a natural resource that replaces imports

questions.questionText: What is likely to explain an increase in the deficit on a country’s current account of the balance of payments?

options.A: an increase in government foreign aid to countries abroad
options.B: an increase in government tax rates
options.C: an increase in other countries’ exchange rates
options.D: an increase in the proportion of income saved by the country’s residents

questions.questionText: What does the Marshall–Lerner condition state must be present for a depreciation of a currency to cause an improvement in the current account balance?

options.A: The price elasticity of demand for exports and the price elasticity of demand for imports are both greater than one.
options.B: The price elasticity of demand for exports and the price elasticity of demand for imports are both less than one.
options.C: The sum of the price elasticity of demand for exports and the price elasticity of demand for imports is greater than one.
options.D: The sum of the price elasticity of demand for exports and the price elasticity of demand for imports is less than one.

questions.questionText: To encourage people to work, a government increases the minimum income level at which people start to pay income tax. Which types of macroeconomic policy are being followed? fiscal monetary supply side policy policy policy
Raising interest rates is proposed to reduce a balance of payments deficit. Which justification for this action is not valid?

options.A: It will attract more foreign currency inflows.
options.B: It will encourage exporters to find new foreign markets.
options.C: It will lower the level of imported consumer goods.
options.D: It will put downward pressure on the exchange rate.
